Welcome to the experiment.

In this experiment you will be solving numerous anagrams (we will explain further soon!).

Before we begin, could you please place your phone out of sight and close any other tabs you have open which may distract you.

You will be quizzed on the following instructions, so it is best to read them carefully!

GANMAAR





The above is an example of an anagram.

It is a word where all the letters have been jumbled up.
Your goal is to unscramble the letters and solve the full word (which coincidentally spells the word ANAGRAM above).

There is only one solution to each anagram in this experiment and you must use all of the letters provided.

None of the words/anagrams displayed will be acronyms or slang for other words.

You will also need to type your answers in CAPITAL LETTERS. So it is best to turn your caps lock key on.

To check you understand the basics of the task, the next page has a practice anagram.

Don't stress if you can't figure it out, not all of the problems will be this difficult.

Press Next to attempt the practice anagram.

In the experiment, anagrams will come in different sets:

RED

BLUE

ORANGE

In the first phase of the experiment you will complete two, three minute runs of each coloured set.
That is, six runs in total (two of each coloured set).

You will be told which set you are doing before each run as well as being reminded of the current set during the run.

After answering an anagram you will receive feedback (i.e., 'correct' or 'wrong') and then a new anagram will be presented.

There is no minimum number of anagrams you need to solve nor a percentage you need to get correct to complete the task.

You will however need to try when solving the anagrams.
For example, do not just enter random letters for every single question.

Some anagrams will be harder than others.

If you can't figure out the answer to an anagram, take a guess and move on.
You won't be penalised for getting one wrong.
